title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
source: canonical Kth Smallest Element in a BST concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the root node of a valid binary search tree and an integer k. Return the k-th smallest value in the tree, counting from 1. The tree ordering means an in-order walk visits values in ascending order.
constraints: the tree is a valid binary search tree

examples.explanation: Ascending order is 1, 3, 4, 5, 8; the 2nd value is 3.
The 4th value in ascending order is 5.

hints: An in-order traversal of a BST visits values in ascending order, so the answer is the k-th stop.
You can stop walking once the counter hits k; the rest of the tree never matters.
Iteratively push left children onto a stack, pop the smallest remaining, count it, and move to its right subtree.
solution: Early-exiting in-order walk: push left children, pop, count, and step right; return the moment the count reaches k. O(k + depth) time, O(depth) stack space.
bruteForceCode:
def kth_smallest(root, k):
    values = []
    stack = []
    node = root
    while stack or node is not None:
        while node is not None:
            stack.append(node)
            node = node.left
        node = stack.pop()
        values.append(node.value)
        node = node.right
    return values[k - 1]
failureHint: hidden tests include the smallest value, the largest value, and single-node trees
